messages.author: 49a67c6e0f03dace
messages.subject: error in scantwo permutation
parts:
Hello Karl!

I tried to run the permutation for scantwo, by using following codes,

try <- read.cross("csvr","","try.csv", na.strings=c("-"),genotypes=c("A","B"),alleles=c("A","B"),estimate.map=F ,"haplotype")
try <- jittermap(try)
try <- calc.genoprob(try, step=1, error.prob=0.001, map.function="kosambi")

map <- pull.map(try)
markers2keep <- lapply(map, pickMarkerSubset, min.distance=0.05)
xsub <- pull.markers(try, unlist(markers2keep))
totmar(xsub)

try <- xsub
try <- calc.genoprob(try, step=1, error.prob=0.001, map.function="kosambi")
operm2 <- scantwo(try,pheno.col=2,method="hk",n.perm = 1000)



but then later I got an error message as followed:

Error in subrousummaryscantwo(tem, for.perm = TRUE) :
  long vectors (argument 3) are not supported in .Fortran
Calls: scantwo ... scantwo.perm.engine -> lapply -> subrousummaryscantwo
Execution halted


This error messages only comes when n.perm=1000. I had tried n.perm=10 and n.perm=100, the tasks were completed successfully.

So how can I solve this problem?

thanks a lot!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] error in scantwo permutation
parts:
No; I would just make ten calls to scantwo().
This might work:

operm2 <- vector(“list”, 10)
for(i in 1:10 P{
   operm2[[i]] <- scantwo(try, pheno.col=2, method=“hk”, n.perm=100)
}
operm2 <- do.call(“rbind”, operm2)

You might also try scantwopermhk, which is a rewrite of the scantwo permutations with method=“hk”, to try to better handle memory.

karl

But due to the limit memory, I can't run the scantwo permutation for 30,000 markers (scantwopermhk also not work with such huge amount of markers).
>
> So my question is: can I use the permutation result from 7000 markers for the stepwiseqtl scan with 30,000 markers? The individual number and the phenotype values are exactly the same for the scantwo permutation and the stepwiseqtl.
>
> Thanks!
>
> On Saturday, January 26, 2019 at 5:01:09 PM UTC+1, Karl Broman wrote:
> Yes you can run multiple traits together, but the memory requirements (and difficulties) increase further.
>
> karl
>
>
> On Sat, Jan 26, 2019 at 9:50 AM ziming zhong <zm.zho...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks a lot Karl for the code! It works well so far!
>
> btw, I also have a simple question: when I run operm2, can I run multiple traits together? I have about 40 traits in one file. So just to save time that i don't have to run the permutation one by one, can I run something like:
>
> operm2 <- scantwo(try, pheno.col=c(2:10), method=“hk”, n.perm=100)
> summary(operm2,alpha=0.05)
>
> By this, will I get the summary of the permutation summary for each trait?
>
> Thanks a lot!!!
>
>
>
>
> On Saturday, January 26, 2019 at 4:19:12 PM UTC+1, Karl Broman wrote:
> No; I would just make ten calls to scantwo().
> This might work:
>
> operm2 <- vector(“list”, 10)
> for(i in 1:10 P{
> operm2[[i]] <- scantwo(try, pheno.col=2, method=“hk”, n.perm=100)
> }
> operm2 <- do.call(“rbind”, operm2)
>
> You might also try scantwopermhk, which is a rewrite of the scantwo permutations with method=“hk”, to try to better handle memory.
>
> karl
>
>
> On Jan 26, 2019, at 9:07 AM, ziming zhong <zm.zho...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>> Something like this?
>>
>> operm2 <- scantwo(try,pheno.col=2,method="hk",n.perm = 1000, batchsize=100, n.cluster=10,)
>>
>> On Saturday, January 26, 2019 at 3:54:02 PM UTC+1, Karl Broman wrote:
>> I would recommend running the permutations in 10 batches of 100, since n.perm=100 works but n.perm=1000 gives an error.
>>
>> karl
>>
>> On Jan 26, 2019, at 8:52 AM, ziming zhong <zm.zho...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>>> Hello Karl!
>>>
>>> I tried to run the permutation for scantwo, by using following codes,
>>>
>>> try <- read.cross("csvr","","try.csv", na.strings=c("-"),genotypes=c("A","B"),alleles=c("A","B"),estimate.map=F ,"haplotype")
>>> try <- jittermap(try)
>>> try <- calc.genoprob(try, step=1, error.prob=0.001, map.function="kosambi")
>>>
>>> map <- pull.map(try)
>>> markers2keep <- lapply(map, pickMarkerSubset, min.distance=0.05)
>>> xsub <- pull.markers(try, unlist(markers2keep))
>>> totmar(xsub)
>>>
>>> try <- xsub
>>> try <- calc.genoprob(try, step=1, error.prob=0.001, map.function="kosambi")
>>> operm2 <- scantwo(try,pheno.col=2,method="hk",n.perm = 1000)
>>>
>>>
>>>
>>> but then later I got an error message as followed:
>>>
>>> Error in subrousummaryscantwo(tem, for.perm = TRUE) :
>>> long vectors (argument 3) are not supported in .Fortran
>>> Calls: scantwo ... scantwo.perm.engine -> lapply -> subrousummaryscantwo
>>> Execution halted
>>>
>>>
>>> This error messages only comes when n.perm=1000. I had tried n.perm=10 and n.perm=100, the tasks were completed successfully.
>>>
>>> So how can I solve this problem?
>>>
>>> thanks a lot!
>>>
